questions.explain: The chapter says the most important things in an actual plan are the gap between estimated and actual row counts, where time is spent, and join-type choice — an operator estimating 1 row but returning 847,523 actual rows means the optimizer is flying blind.
options: The query text length
The difference between estimated and actual row counts
The alphabetical order of operators
The number of pages in the buffer pool
questions.q: When reading an actual execution plan, what is the single most important red flag to look for?

questions.explain: The chapter says parameter sniffing compiles a plan from the first call's parameter values and caches it; a later call with very different values gets a catastrophically wrong plan, and fixes include OPTION (RECOMPILE), OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN, plan guides, or forcing a good plan through Query Store.
options: It disables the plan cache entirely
A stored procedure's cached plan, compiled from the first call's parameter values, performs catastrophically for later calls with very different values
It forces every query to use snapshot isolation
It makes statistics auto-update run continuously
questions.q: What is parameter sniffing, and which remedies does the chapter name?

questions.explain: The chapter explains auto-update fires when ~20% of rows change (TF 2371 lowers this dynamically for large tables), but statistics aren't updated continuously, so on high-write tables they can lag badly behind reality.
options: Statistics are always current on any table
Auto-update triggers at 50% row change
Auto-update fires when roughly 20% of rows change, but statistics are not updated continuously, so high-write tables can outrun them
The default resolution is 1000 histogram buckets
questions.q: When does auto-update statistics fire, and what is its limitation on high-write tables?

questions.explain: The chapter says modern guidance is to raise cost threshold from the ancient default of 5 to 25–50 and set MAXDOP per workload (often 4–8 for OLTP), since parallelism adds exchange-operator overhead on fast 2ms queries.
options: Raise cost threshold for parallelism from 5 to 25–50 and set MAXDOP per workload
Set MAXDOP to 0 for all OLTP workloads
Lower cost threshold to 1 so every query runs in parallel
Disable parallelism with OPTION (MAXDOP 1) on all queries
questions.q: What is the chapter's modern guidance for cost threshold for parallelism and MAXDOP?

questions.explain: The chapter says function-wrapped columns and implicit type conversions (e.g., filtering a VARCHAR column with an integer literal, forcing a convert of every value) both break index seeks and require rewrites — check the plan for CONVERT_IMPLICIT warnings.
options: They make the query non-SARGable
They disable statistics auto-update
They force a nested loops join
Function-wrapped columns and implicit conversions break index seeks; the fixes are rewriting so the column is bare and matching data types
questions.q: How do function-wrapped columns and implicit type conversions affect index usage in SQL Server?
